item.title: Is there a canon history of The Foundation?: Re: Is there a canon history of The Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
So, is there a list of sites and do they have specialisation?

There is, but people pay attention to/ignore them as they feel.

On a given article, might get pushback from one or two people claiming that Site 437 is only for the containment of crocodilian objects or that Site 28 is for the assessment of gas-based SCP objects. Ignore this criticism, as it is pedantry disguising itself as analysis and is fundamentally unserious.

In terms of general history, not really. There are loads of different interpretations of how it was founded, when, where, why, and by who, but none of them are any more correct than any other. In fact, there's even a canon in which there is no Foundation. Go wild.

item.title: Can I create an scp that was made by an object related to an scp?: Re: Can I create an scp that was made by an object related to an scp?
item.content:encoded:
There's two parts to your answer:

Are you allowed to do this: Yes. Pretty much anything on the site is fair game for stuff like this.

Will people respond well to this: This is the tricky part. The item will have to stand on its own both in-universe and out-of-universe. In-universe, there would have to be a reason for the item to have its own SCP documentation- it'd have to be an independent anomaly with its own special procedures or unique traits that isn't better filed as an addendum to a parent article. Out-of-universe, derivative SCPs are like movie sequels: the good ones tell their own story beyond the original(s), while also justifying the connection as more than just an attempt to piggyback on name recognition.

item.title: SCP Number: Re: SCP Number
item.content:encoded: As laid out in the How to Write an SCP guide, the number is picked when you choose which open slot to put your SCP in when you post it. This is likely to be within Series 6, though some slots in earlier series may be open.
